definition: An `input_wires` entry routes a face to an immediate child's face. An `output_wires` entry sources a face from an immediate child's face. An entry of any of the three is a wire
note: g-entry lists table, input, executor, roster, batch and condition entries but no wiring entry; §13.3:10342 and Appendix C:13871 use the bare phrase and §6.1 defines it only implicitly, so add the sense.

definition: Condition entries are validated in the collecting form
note: Already listed in g-entry (cites §14.3), though §14.1:11426 is the first use and §14.3 flattening gives the flat form; confirm the citation and add a gloss: one path-addressed write of a condition.

definition: the producer's declared type must be a subtype of the consumer's input entry
note: Already listed in g-entry (cites §8.2) but first used at §6.1:1596, before its cited section; consider a gloss: a consumer's `u_types` entry, tolerant or Pinned.

definition: A tap names one scalar
note: The g-taps entry already says every tap names one scalar; singular tap and x-/u-/y-tap are the element of the tap set, so no new entry.

definition: The stopped-sim services are initialization, the overlay, trim, linearization, and `checkpoint` with its partner `restore!`.
note: Used about 57 times across chapters 1 to 14 with no anchor (g-service-lifecycle only covers the error); the definition sits in the §14 intro and in the §9.6 heading. Draft: the services that run on a non-running simulation: init!, overlay!, trim!, linearize, checkpoint and restore!.

definition: The start of a frame is its frame top.
note: Over 100 uses, defined once in §2.1 and used in every runtime chapter; g-boundary and g-frame only mention it. Draft: the start of a frame, a grid boundary where the drain runs and a legal halt for checkpoint, replay and stop.

definition: The first honoured request reading `STOP_REQUESTED` initiates §12.4 shutdown with *this* snapshot as the final one. The terminal snapshot is the terminal state.
note: Eleven uses over §11 to §13 and defined in §12.4 (outside my range); g-snapshot lacks it. Could instead be a sense of snapshot. Draft: the final published snapshot of a run, carrying its last cumulative counters; no roll-back.

definition: The service walk follows the structure's children and refuses no traversal past a generically held child
note: Seven uses, bold-defined in §13.3 and used in §14.4 and the client table; names the resolution rule for services, readers and bindings. Draft: the path resolution that follows the structure's children, refusing no traversal past a generically held child, applied to every client except wiring.

definition: The one-level rule covers all three wiring declarations.
note: Ten uses (also "one-level routing") over five sections and defined in §6.1, far from its §13.3 and §14.2 uses; no anchor. Draft: a connection endpoint resolves to an immediate child and one of its faces; a path reaching further is a PathResolution error.

definition: locality law ([D-065][d-065]). Fragments of the condition algebra follow the same law
note: Listed in bucket D of the inventory, but now seven uses in six sections with its third instance in §14.2:11572; promote. Draft: each level speaks its own fields, its declared children's names and its own faces; holds for local wires, interface connections and conditions.

definition: The build's steps are barriers ([D-259]). A step that produced any error-severity diagnostic, from either population, throws before the next step begins.
note: Used in §13.1, §13.2 and Appendix C with no anchor; the carrier of the collected throw. Draft: a build step that throws, merged over every pass that ran, before the next step begins.

definition: Collection reaches the step barrier, under a dependency rule. A declarative pass runs when the results it reads are clean.
note: Two body uses in one section plus Appendix C; pair with step barrier but an inline gloss suffices.

definition: The code inside the `Model`'s `try` is the guarded sequence.
note: Three uses by rule, all inside §13.4 within about 30 lines and also in the boundary-zero and species passages; a local gloss would do, so the orchestrator may demote to D.

definition: A user-code exception is wrapped in a framing diagnostic, `UserCodeFraming`, with the original exception as `cause`.
note: Nine uses; first use in §9.3 cites forward to §13.2, so defined far from some uses. Draft: wrapping a user-code exception in UserCodeFraming with the component path, function and probe context, original as cause; the framed set is every user-authored method.

definition: That unwrapping is the species rule.
note: The g-species entry already states the rule ("under the species rule"); the coinage is its alias.

definition: the cursor frame (the cursor's copy at the catch)
note: The execution-cursor entry already says a failure gets its cursor frame.

definition: The frame-entry boundary index is the replay pointer
note: Name for StepError's frame-entry boundary index; defined here but used in §9.5, §10.4 and §12.7. g-replay is the nearest anchor; a short clause there may suffice, or promote to C.

definition: The ignore list, `ignore_stop_requests`, sits beside `t_end` at the same declaration site.
note: g-stop-policy already covers the ignored requester paths and the ignore mask; both coinages are aliases.

definition: naming how the run ended) as the tail residue
note: Already named in g-termination-record's text, so an alias, though defined in §11.8 and used in §13.5 and §12.4.

definition: The protocol becomes one tail with two entry points. Graceful entry follows a *completed* final boundary, and abnormal entry follows a *discarded* one.
note: A further sense of entry (a way into the shutdown tail); g-entry's list lacks it.

definition: The abnormal path discards the failed boundary, promotes the previous snapshot to final, and rejoins the ordinary tail
note: The loop's shutdown protocol of §12.4 (outside my range) is named "the tail" across §11 to §13 with no anchor; the count of 26 is noisy because "the tail" is also ordinary English, so verify. Draft: the shutdown sequence after the final snapshot: sticky stopped, waiters woken, unblock! and shutdown!, named joins with timeout.

definition: the address table: a cell the structure has
note: Four uses in two sections, defined in the §13.3 client table and used by inspection; inline gloss.

definition: After *every* published boundary the loop scans the `StopFlag` block of the snapshot it just published
note: Two uses; the g-stop-request entry carries the content.

definition: The probe-value barrier is structural. ... The services path simply contains no call to it.
note: Three uses by rule, defined in §14.6 and already described in g-probe-value's text as "a structural barrier"; may be an alias, so B is also defensible.

definition: A would-be init value that depends on swept outputs is either analytically known to the caller or an equilibrium constraint. This is the pre-sweep doctrine
note: Four uses, with §14.7 citing §14.1; also gets a D.8 entry candidate. Draft: a condition value that depends on swept outputs is either known to the caller or an equilibrium constraint for trim.

definition: A leaf already at the activation's scalar type is decision-descended.
note: Four uses in two sections, one table; inline gloss.

definition: The second is the walk clause, for a continuous consumer only.
note: Eight uses, defined at §6.1 and §8.2 and used in §13.7:11132 far from both; no anchor beyond g-walked. Draft: a producer's walking leaf may feed a consumer entry only if the consumer is tolerant; a pinned entry refuses it.

definition: | `Float64`, alone or as a type parameter | tolerant | the activation scalar or a frozen `Float64` |
note: Twelve uses; g-walked explains Pinned and says what a consumer's entry "tolerates" but never names a tolerant entry. Could be folded into g-walked as a B alias.

definition: The export chain is the
note: Seven uses; first defined in §11.7 (a GUI passage), used in §14.2 and §14.9 far from it. Draft: the chain of faces a signal crosses at each assembly level up to a root input.

definition: `show(::Structure)` owes face routes
note: Six uses, nearly all in §13.7; inline gloss.

definition: The diagnostic lists every dead hop under either verdict
note: Ten uses; §13.8:11303 gives the sense but §5.4 uses it earlier. Draft: a hop inside a member where the stage-2 map does not route the entering face to the leaving port.

definition: The remedy ladder for
note: Three uses in three chapters, defined at §5.4 and reused far away in §10.2:5652 for stiffness. Draft: the ordered fixes offered for an artificial loop: split the component or narrow a neighbor's contract.

definition: The frozen-exact doctrine is consumer-scoped, not a capability wall.
note: Three uses, but §8.6 only as a comment; an inline gloss near §7.2 and §14.10 suffices.

definition: A `Pinned` entry is the FFI door. This input must never carry partials.
note: Two paired coinages (the input half and the output half of non-participation), five uses between §8.2 and §14.10; defined in §8.2, used in §14.10:12994 far away. Draft: the Pinned marker; FFI door refuses partials at an input, freeze door declares an output frozen under differentiation.

definition: `committed_residuals` are the committed-state residuals, the same residuals re-gathered from the boundary-zero world after the commit.
note: Thirteen uses, all of the trim report; the term pairs with TrimCommitResiduals and TrimCommitChecks. Draft: residuals and checks re-gathered from the boundary-zero world after the commit, so they describe the state the simulation is in.

definition: prepends the prefix to the set's mount chain (the prefixes it is mounted under, root first)
note: Four uses, all in one section; inline gloss already given. Alias of g-mounting detail.

definition: the level a problem's or tap set's reads are mounted at
note: A part of mounting already glossed in §14.4:11814; alias.

definition: thin rigs (worlds holding only the aircraft and its environment)
note: Five uses, defined in §14.9 with design_world as its named instance; may be an alias of g-design_world or g-component-test-rig.

definition: `reads` is the declared read set.
note: Twenty-one uses and a `Reads` value type; g-selector covers the selectors but not the set. Draft: the declared set of named selector reads of a trim problem or tap set, carrying its mount chain.

definition: A selector resolves against a source. ... The table selectors ... resolve against a *table source*.
note: Both are described inside g-selector's text (table source, live stores); alias.

term: global tracer / sampled tracer / tracer tags
definition: The *global* (value-blind) set-tracer is a `Real` subtype ... The *sampled* set-tracer
note: The tracer's two modes are already summarized in g-feedthrough-tracer; alias.

definition: the *list-in-hand* a did-you-mean needs
note: Part of g-did-you-mean's own definition.

definition: compiled readers are the gather twin
note: Two uses; inline gloss.

definition: runs one establishment round
note: Two uses in one passage; inline gloss.

definition: That is the no-silent-zeros rule ([§9.5][s9-5]).
note: Two uses; inline gloss.

definition: A condition applied through `init!` overlays the declared defaults
note: Two uses; inline gloss.
